attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase used to create noun-like phrases, or sometimes ask questions about what (A) means.

attributes.body:
One of the ways to perform nominalization (turning a phrase into a noun) in Japanese is through the use of the expression ということ. This grammar point is a combination of と (the particle), 言（い）う (the verb), and こと (the noun). Together, the literal translation is close to 'that (A) is said to be'. However, in reality, it sounds far less formal than this.

To use ということ, attach it to the end of any phrase (without です, or ます). In most cases it will be written using hiragana.

In conversation, という is regularly shortened to simply って. This form will be heard/seen much more frequently in conversation/manga and similar things.

ということ is also frequently used when clarifying what someone else has said. In these cases, it translates very similarly to 'you mean that (A)?', or 'you mean to say that (A)?'

Caution

Although the kanji 言（い）う and 事（こと） may be used in this expression, the most common form does not use any kanji at all. This is a regular occurence in Japanese, as many set grammatical structures will not use kanji, simply because it makes the pattern easier to identify.

attributes.description: ということ Example Sentences with Audio

attributes.body: ということ turns phrases into nouns and often clarifies what was said, e.g. 日本に行くということ 'the fact that he's going to Japan'. Adding だ forms ということだ, which is used to report information second-hand, e.g. 来年から海外に住むということだ ('I hear he'll be living abroad from next year.').

second_relatable.title: ということだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

attributes.body: ということ turns phrases into nouns and is often used to clarify what was said. When followed by は as ということは, it marks the phrase as a topic for further explanation or comment. ということは can also begin a sentence to restate or interpret what came before, like 'So what you're saying is (A)' in English.

second_relatable.title: ということは
second_relatable.meaning: That means, That is to say

attributes.body: ことなの combines こと with the explanatory ～んです／のです form and is used to give or ask for background with an emphatic, explanatory tone. ということ also turns a phrase into a noun, meaning 'the fact that' or 'the act of (A)', but is typically used to clarify something without the added emphasis of ん／の.

first_relatable.title: ことなの
first_relatable.meaning: (A) is (Description of A), (A) means that (Description of A)

attributes.body: ということ turns phrases into nouns and is often used to clarify or restate something, e.g. 日本に行くということ 'the fact that (he) is going to Japan'. という by itself links a phrase or name to a noun, as in ポチという犬 'a dog named Pochi' or 来年日本に行くという学生 'a student who is going to Japan'.

second_relatable.title: という
second_relatable.meaning: Called, Named, Known as, As much as

attributes.body: ということ and というのは both turn phrases into nouns. ということ is often used to clarify what was said, while というのは introduces a topic for further explanation or comment. というのは can also start a sentence to mean 'what I mean is (A)' or 'that is to say (A)'.

second_relatable.title: というのは
second_relatable.meaning: ~ Known as ~ is, ~ Called ~ is, ~ Means ~, Because

attributes.body: こと attaches to the dictionary form of verbs to turn them into nouns, e.g. 行くこと '(the act of) going'. ということ has a similar function, but adds the quoting phrase という, so it's often used to clarify information or reported speech, e.g. 日本に行くということ 'the fact that (he) is going to Japan'.
